title: Honen and His Followers Distort and Slander Master Shandao
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Question: It is said that Master Honen “personally founded the Pure Land school on the basis of the Pure Land thought of Master Shandao, an emanation of Amitabha Buddha.” Is that so?

inline.s: Question: It is said that Master Honen “personally founded the Pure Land school on the basis of the Pure Land thought of Master Shandao, an emanation of Amitabha Buddha.” Is that so?
Answer: Master Shandao has long been wronged! This is Honen and his followers raising a great banner to serve as a tiger’s skin, wrapping themselves in it to frighten people and deceive them.

First let us look at the true face of “Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought,” and then at the “Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought” spoken of by Honen and his followers, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others.
Below is the record concerning Master Shandao in the Record of Pure Land Sages and Worthies (for a full vernacular translation, see
“The Life of Master Shandao (Vernacular and Original Text)”
Tang Dynasty
Shandao (Second Patriarch of the Lotus school)
Shandao, whose origins are unknown
(his background is unclear)
. During the Zhenguan era
(the Zhenguan years of Emperor Taizong of Tang)
, he saw the Pure Land nine-grade practice hall of Master Chuo of Xihe
(Master Daochuo)
, and rejoiced, saying: ‘This is truly the ford and essential point for entering the Buddha’s way
(the essential path)
. To cultivate other practices is roundabout and hard to accomplish; only this Dharma gate quickly transcends birth and death.’
Thereupon he became diligent, earnest, and austere, bowing and reciting day and night
. Soon
(before long)
he reached the capital and inspired the four assemblies
(encouraging and teaching the four assemblies to practice Buddha-recitation)
. Whenever he entered his room, he would kneel long and chant the Buddha’s name,
never stopping until his strength was exhausted
. Coming out, he would expound the Pure Land Dharma gate.
For more than thirty years he never slept
He guarded and upheld the precepts, not transgressing even a hair’s breadth
. Fine food he gave to the assembly; coarse and poor fare he kept for himself. All the gifts
chèn
he received
(all the offerings and gifts he received)
he used to copy more than a hundred thousand fascicles of the Amitabha Sutra
, to paint three hundred wall panels of Pure Land transformation scenes, to build and repair stupas and temples, and to light lamps and keep the light burning
(lighting bright lamps as offerings to the Buddha)
. Monastics and laity
(monks and laypeople)
who followed his teaching were very numerous
(whether renunciate or householder, those who followed him and received his teaching were extremely many)

, some reciting the Amitabha Sutra ten thousand to five hundred thousand times, some daily reciting the Buddha’s name from ten thousand to a hundred thousand times. Among them, those who attained samādhi and were reborn in the Pure Land cannot be recorded
(they were so many that they could not be recorded or described)
Someone asked: ‘Does Buddha-recitation bring rebirth in the Pure Land?’ Shandao replied: ‘As you recite, so shall your wish be fulfilled
(as you recite the Buddha’s name with diligence, your aspiration to be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss will surely be fulfilled)
.’ Then
(thereupon)
he recited once himself, and a light came forth from his mouth; ten times up to a hundred, the light was likewise
(thereby proving that the merit of Buddha-recitation is true and not vain)
His verse exhorting the world says: ‘Gradually the skin wrinkles and the hair turns white; soon the step falters and the gait grows feeble. Even
(even if)
with gold and jade filling the hall, how can one escape
(could one really escape)
decline, decay, sickness, and suffering? However many pleasures you enjoy, impermanence will come in the end. Only the direct path of practice
(only by practicing along the most direct and convenient path)
, simply reciting Amitābha Buddha.’

Someone asked: ‘Why not have people cultivate visualization, but instead send them straight to exclusive recitation of the name?’ He answered: ‘Living beings have heavy obstructions, the objects are subtle and the mind is coarse, the consciousness wavers and the spirit flies
(the mind-consciousness stirs and the spirit scatters)
, so visualization is hard to accomplish. Therefore the Great Sage
(Śākyamuni Buddha)
in his compassion directly urged exclusive recitation of the name. Precisely because recitation of the name is easy,
with continuity one is immediately reborn
. If one can
keep thought after thought continuous, with the end of life as the limit
, then ten out of ten are reborn, a hundred out of a hundred are reborn. Why? Because without outer mixed conditions, one attains right mindfulness
(because the mind does not reach out after this and that, and right mindfulness continues without interruption)
because one accords with the Buddha’s original vow
(because one accords with Amitābha Buddha’s original vow)
; because one does not contradict the teachings; because one follows the Buddha’s words.
‘If one forsakes exclusive recitation and cultivates mixed practices, scarcely one or two in a hundred succeed, scarcely three or four in a thousand.
Why? Because mixed conditions stir and disorder the mind
(because the mind reaches out after this and that)
, and right mindfulness is lost; because one does not accord with the Buddha’s original vow; because one contradicts the teachings; because one does not follow the Buddha’s words;
because mindfulness is not continuous
because the mind does not continue in mindfulness and so does not repay the Buddha’s kindness

; because although one performs karmic practices, one is constantly in accord with fame and profit; because one delights in approaching mixed conditions, thereby obstructing oneself and others in the right practice of rebirth.
Recently
(lately)

I have seen monastics and laity in all regions whose understanding and practice differ, and who differ in exclusivity and mixture. But those who practice with single-minded intent—ten out of ten are reborn. Those who cultivate mixed practices without reaching the mind’s core—not one in a thousand.
May all people reflect well; whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, they must steel the mind and master themselves, never slackening day or night, with the end of life as the limit

. When the former thought ends, at the next thought one is reborn; for long ages and endless kalpas one enjoys the bliss of the unconditioned Dharma, until one attains Buddhahood—is that not delightful!’

He also wrote a text on right mindfulness at the time of death, saying: ‘When an ordinary person is about to die and wishes to be reborn in the Pure Land, they must not be afraid of death. They should constantly reflect that this body has much suffering, impure and evil conditions, entangled in countless ways. If one can abandon this filthy body, transcend birth into the Pure Land, receive immeasurable happiness, and be freed from the bitter destinies of birth and death, that is a matter for rejoicing. It is like taking off worn-out clothes and getting to put on precious garments.

Let go of body and mind, and do not give rise to attachment. As soon as illness comes, reflect on impermanence and single-mindedly await death. You must instruct your family and those who come to inquire, whoever comes before you, to recite the Buddha’s name for you. They must not speak idle and miscellaneous words about the present, nor about the long and short affairs of the household. Nor need they comfort you with soft words and wish you peace and happiness, for all of that is vain and profitless. If the illness is grave and death is near,
your relatives must not shed tears or weep, nor utter sighs and sounds of regret, confusing the mind and spirit and causing the loss of right mindfulness
. Simply have them keep Amitābha Buddha in mind and guard it until the breath is gone.
If one can have people who clearly understand the Pure Land come frequently to encourage and urge one on, that is a very great fortune. By this method one will certainly be reborn; have no doubt.
The matter of birth and death is grave; only one’s own effort will avail. If a single thought goes wrong at the time of death, one suffers for kalpas—who can bear it in your place?
(if a single thought goes wrong at the time of death, the consequence is suffering for kalpas—who can bear it in your place?)
Think of it! Think of it!
One day Shandao suddenly said to the people
This body is loathsome; I shall return to the West.
Then he climbed the willow tree in front of the temple and, facing west, made this vow
May the Buddha receive me, may the bodhisattvas aid me,
so that I do not lose right mindfulness
, and attain rebirth in the Land of Peace and Nurture.
Having spoken, he threw himself down and passed away. Emperor Gaozong knew of his wondrous powers and bestowed upon the temple a plaque reading
Guangming
it is said
(Emperor Gaozong of Tang knew that Master Shandao’s practice was wondrous and unfathomable, and therefore bestowed on the temple a plaque
inscribed with the name
Guangming
From this biography we can see that Master Shandao’s words, deeds, and positions include the following points:
1. Strict and meticulous observance of the precepts.
2. Diligent Buddha-recitation.
3. Vigorously advocating the upholding of the Buddha Speaks the Amitabha Sutra.
4. With continuity, one is immediately reborn.
5. Right mindfulness at the time of death.
6. The matter of birth and death is grave; only one’s own effort will avail.

There is one more point: the two practices, primary and auxiliary. This is set out in the Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra in Four Fascicles, which was lost in China and later returned; there Master Shandao specifically explained the two practices, primary and auxiliary, by which the Pure Land school cultivates. Here Master Shandao strongly emphasizes single-mindedness: whether reciting sutras, recollecting, bowing to the Buddha, or holding the name, whether praising or making offerings,
all must be single-minded—this is the key to correct practice
. Single-mindedness means the mind’s focus is undivided and undistracted. The original text is as follows:

Now practice is of two kinds: first, primary practice; second, mixed practice. Primary practice means exclusively relying on the rebirth sutras in one’s practice—this is called primary practice. What are they?
Single-mindedly
and exclusively read and recite this Contemplation Sutra, the Amitabha Sutra, the Immeasurable Life Sutra, and so on;
single-mindedly
and exclusively focus the mind on contemplating, observing, and recollecting the adornments of the two kinds of reward in that land. If bowing, then
single-mindedly
bow exclusively to that Buddha; if reciting aloud, then
single-mindedly
recite exclusively that Buddha’s name; if praising and making offerings, then
single-mindedly
praise and make offerings exclusively; this is called primary. Again, within this primary there are two further kinds: first,

single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting the name of Amitābha, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, regardless of whether the time be long or short, never forsaking it thought after thought—this is called the karma of settled certainty

, because it accords with that Buddha’s vow; if one relies on bowing, reciting, and the like, that is called auxiliary karma. Apart from these two practices, primary and auxiliary, all other virtues are called mixed practice. If one cultivates the former two practices, primary and auxiliary, the mind is constantly close and recollection is unbroken—this is called uninterrupted.
In summary, Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought is:

strict and meticulous observance of the precepts, diligent Buddha-recitation, upholding the Buddha Speaks the Amitabha Sutra and practicing according to its teaching, with continuity one is immediately reborn, right mindfulness at the time of death, the matter of birth and death is grave and only one’s own effort will avail, and the two practices, primary and auxiliary.
Master Yinguang praised him, saying:

“Monk Shandao was an emanation of Amitabha, possessing great spiritual powers and great wisdom. In his propagation of the Pure Land, he did not esteem the abstruse and wondrous, but only taught people to cultivate in what is true, earnest, ordinary, and practical.”
(“Letter in Reply to a Certain Lay Buddhist of Yongjia and His Brothers”)

Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others among Honen’s followers repeatedly claim that Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought was lost in our country, and that only Honen and his like in Japan inherited this Pure Land orthodoxy. In fact, which of the patriarchs and great masters of the Pure Land school in our country did not advocate

“strict and meticulous observance of the precepts, diligent Buddha-recitation, upholding the Buddha Speaks the Amitabha Sutra and practicing according to its teaching, with continuity one is immediately reborn, right mindfulness at the time of death, the matter of birth and death is grave and only one’s own effort will avail, and the two practices, primary and auxiliary”
? Which of them did not lead by example, put it into practice, and truly cultivate and truly realize?
Now let us look again at the “Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought” spoken of by Honen and his followers, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others:

1. Master Shandao led by example, observing the precepts strictly and meticulously, guarding and upholding the precepts without transgressing even a hair’s breadth. Yet Honen and his followers, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others, preach: recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth; there is no need to observe precepts, no need to cultivate merit, no need to purify one’s own mind—even a lifetime of evildoing does not matter. And they say “evil people are the true recipients.” Master Huijing says in The Essential Meaning of Master Shandao: “It is not known that the purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to reveal Amitābha’s original vow—evil people are the true recipients.” Master Xinyuan, a disciple of Master Huijing who took refuge, says: “Let us now look at Amitābha Buddha’s deliverance: for what kind of living being is it the true recipient? Evil people are the true recipients.” Our teacher Śākyamuni Buddha proclaimed with his golden mouth, and Amitābha Buddha of the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss praised and embraced, the
Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception
which says:
“Not by slight roots of goodness can any sentient being attain rebirth in the pure buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha Immeasurable Life.”
Yet the original-vow Dharma gate recklessly preaches “evil people are the true recipients”—to such an extent does it slander the Buddha and destroy the Dharma!

[Roots of goodness] means the goodness of the three karmas of body, speech, and mind; because they can produce wondrous fruit, they are called roots. [Sentient being] is also called living being, that is, every creature that has consciousness.

2. Master Shandao led by example, reciting the Buddha’s name diligently, earnest and austere, bowing and reciting day and night. Yet Honen and his followers, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others, preach: recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth. Therefore it is enough to recite casually. They even say: rebirth depends entirely on the Buddha’s power; Amitābha Buddha practices in our place and bears our karmic offenses.

3. Master Shandao vigorously advocated upholding the Buddha Speaks the Amitabha Sutra, personally copying more than a hundred thousand fascicles to distribute to his disciples and the faithful, requiring them to practice according to its teaching: with single-mindedness undefiled, the Buddha will surely come to welcome them. The Tang translation of the Buddha Speaks the Amitabha Sutra, the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception, has the World-Honored One teaching in that sutra: with uninterrupted mindfulness (single-mindedness undefiled), the Buddha will surely come to welcome them. Yet Master Honen actually distorted the sutra text into: “Because one constantly recites the Buddha’s name, the Buddha will surely come to welcome one.” (For details see the article
“Master Honen Distorts the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception”

.) What is more, in the “threefold abolition and establishment” propagated by Honen and his followers, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others, they even frenziedly clamor to “abandon the nineteenth vow, the twentieth vow, and the provisional means of the Contemplation Sutra and the Amitabha Sutra, and to establish the true and real of the eighteenth vow of the Immeasurable Life Sutra.” (For details see the article
“The Original-Vow Dharma Gate Is a Heretical Path”

Openly slandering the Amitabha Sutra, praised by the buddhas of the ten directions (which of course includes Amitābha Buddha of the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss), as a “provisional means” to be abolished! Could this be Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought?
4. Master Shandao taught: with continuity, one is immediately reborn (for details see the article
“With Continuity, One Is Immediately Reborn”

). Yet Honen and his followers, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others, preach: “Recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth.” They even say: “Rebirth through scattered-mind Buddha-recitation is precisely the supreme original vow.”

5. Master Shandao admonished those who recite the Buddha’s name that they must certainly maintain right mindfulness at the time of death, and said with incomparable earnestness: “If a single thought goes wrong, one suffers for kalpas—who can bear it in your place? (If a single thought goes wrong at the time of death, the consequence is suffering for kalpas—who can bear it in your place?) Think of it! Think of it!” (For details see the article
“Annotations to ‘Monk Shandao’s Text on Right Mindfulness for Rebirth at the Time of Death’”

). Yet Honen and his followers, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others, say: “‘Right mindfulness at the time of death, the Buddha comes to welcome one’—this view is wrong; ‘the Buddha comes to welcome one, and so one abides in right mindfulness’—this is right.” (For details see the article
“Master Honen Distorts the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception”
6. Master Shandao admonished those who recite the Buddha’s name: “The matter of birth and death is grave; only one’s own effort will avail.” (For details see the article
“Annotations to ‘Monk Shandao’s Text on Right Mindfulness for Rebirth at the Time of Death’”

). Yet Honen and his followers, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others, recklessly preach: rebirth depends entirely on the Buddha’s power; Amitābha Buddha practices in our place and bears our karmic offenses.

7. In the Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra in Four Fascicles, Master Shandao specifically taught the two practices, primary and auxiliary, by which the Pure Land school cultivates. (For annotations see the article
“Master Shandao’s Pure Land Teaching”

.) Master Honen not only failed to apply himself steadily to the two practices, primary and auxiliary, by which the Pure Land school cultivates as taught by Master Shandao (this is Master Shandao’s Pure Land teaching), and to teach his disciples and the faithful in this way, but instead distorted Master Shandao’s teaching in the Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra in Four Fascicles, fabricating a “gate of the vast vow” of his own, claiming: the founder of the gate of essential teaching is Śākyamuni Buddha, and the founder of the gate of the vast vow is Amitābha Buddha, and “abolishing the essential and establishing the vast vow” (abolishing the gate of essential teaching and establishing the gate of the vast vow). He even framed Master Shandao, saying this was Master Shandao’s own classification. (For details see the article
“Master Honen Fabricates the Gate of the Vast Vow”

In summary, we clearly see that Honen and his followers, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others, have completely violated Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought; they are diametrically opposing Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought. Yet in order to deceive the faithful, they repeatedly claim: they revere Master Shandao, and what they speak is “Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought”!
Just look at the video of “Master Shandao’s Pure Land Thought” lectured by Master Jingzong, and you will know.
In his lecture on
Master Shandao’s Pure Land Thought
, Master Jingzong says again and again that
the “gate of the vast vow” and “recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth” are the core of Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought. But what are the facts?
Master Shandao never spoke of a gate of the vast vow at all; this was entirely fabricated by Master Honen
(for details see the article
“Master Honen Fabricates the Gate of the Vast Vow”
. Nor did Master Shandao ever say that recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth; on the contrary, Master Shandao said: with continuity, one is immediately reborn
(for details see the article
“Master Shandao’s Pure Land Teaching”

The “gate of the vast vow” and “recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth” that they fabricated themselves, they then forcibly attribute to Master Shandao, falsely claiming this is Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought. Is this how one reveres Master Shandao? Is this how one propagates Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought?
Master Shandao has three extremely important teachings: 1. the two practices, primary and auxiliary; 2. with continuity, one is immediately reborn; 3. right mindfulness at the time of death.
(For details see
“Master Shandao’s Pure Land Teaching”
the article
In these three teachings, Master Shandao clearly expounds how one can be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss; this is
Master Shandao’s Pure Land teaching
. Yet in the “sayings of Master Shandao” compiled by Master Huijing and Master Jingzong
(for details see The Complete Works of Master Shandao, compiled and narrated by Master Huijing and Master Jingzong, published in 2005 by Jingzong Publishing House)
they
do not dare to include them

, fearing that their true colors would be exposed. This fully proves that their reliance on Master Shandao is false, and that they merely raise the banner of “reliance” to peddle their own goods; it also fully proves that the “Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought” they propagate is not the true Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought.

These three teachings of Master Shandao (“the two practices, primary and auxiliary,” “with continuity, one is immediately reborn,” and “right mindfulness at the time of death”) are a demon-revealing mirror. Set the statements of Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others alongside them, and whether they rely on Master Shandao, whether they propagate Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought, whether they propagate Master Shandao’s Dharma gate of Buddha-recitation—whether true or false, orthodox or heretical—is instantly clear.
Question: Master Shandao said: recitation of the name is the karma of settled certainty. Therefore, recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth. Is that so?
Answer: In the Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra in Four Fascicles, Master Shandao says this:
Single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting
the name of Amitābha, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, regardless of whether the time be long or short,
never forsaking it thought after thought
, is called the karma of settled certainty.”
Please note that in this teaching, “
single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting
” and “
never forsaking it thought after thought

”—this is what makes it the karma of settled certainty. Yet these people altered this teaching into: “Recitation of the name is the karma of settled certainty.” One of the habitual tactics of Honen and his followers, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others, is to cut off the head and tail, take passages out of context, and tamper at will; therefore when reading their works and statements you must be extremely careful, and at key points you must certainly compare them with the original text.
[Settled certainty] correct meditative concentration. When body and mind are pure and undefiled and undistracted, it is called “settled certainty.” [Karma] the activity of body, speech, and mind.
Question: If a statement does not indicate its source, how am I to check it against the original text?

Answer: To quote sutras, treatises, and the teachings of the patriarchs without appending the original text and without indicating the source is an extremely irresponsible practice. Of course, this is also where their cunning lies, using it to pass off the false as genuine. Still, you can search online to verify it.
Question: Master Shandao said: recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth. Is that so?

Answer: Quite the contrary—Master Shandao said: uninterrupted mindfulness invariably brings rebirth (with continuity, one is immediately reborn), right mindfulness at the time of death invariably brings rebirth, and single-mindedness undefiled invariably brings rebirth.
Question: Please explain in detail.

Answer: “Uninterrupted mindfulness invariably brings rebirth (with continuity, one is immediately reborn)” means: the thought of Buddha-recitation continues thought after thought, and at the end of life one immediately attains rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. “Continuity” here is what the Chapter on the Perfect Penetration of Buddha-Recitation by Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta calls “pure mindfulness in succession,” that is, the thought of Buddha-recitation continues thought after thought with no idle thoughts intermingled (if idle thoughts are intermingled, it is not continuity); this then is the state of single-mindedness undefiled (uninterrupted mindfulness). Never misunderstand the two words “continuity” here as meaning that the sound of the Buddha’s name continues aloud (while the mind is mixed with idle thoughts). As the saying goes, a difference of a hair’s breadth becomes an error of a thousand miles. (For details see the article
“With Continuity, One Is Immediately Reborn”

“Right mindfulness at the time of death invariably brings rebirth” means: if at the time of death one can maintain right mindfulness of Buddha-recitation, one will certainly be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. If right mindfulness is lost, one cannot be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. Therefore Master Shandao earnestly admonished: “If a single thought goes wrong, one suffers for kalpas—who can bear it in your place? (If a single thought goes wrong at the time of death, the consequence is suffering for kalpas—who can bear it in your place?) Think of it! Think of it!” (For details see the article
“Annotations to ‘Monk Shandao’s Text on Right Mindfulness for Rebirth at the Time of Death’”

“Single-mindedness undefiled invariably brings rebirth” was proclaimed by Śākyamuni Buddha in the Buddha Speaks the Amitabha Sutra (the Tang translation being the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception), and is praised and embraced by the buddhas of the ten directions (which of course includes Amitābha Buddha of the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss). Therefore Master Shandao personally copied more than a hundred thousand fascicles of the Amitabha Sutra and distributed them to his disciples and the faithful, requiring them to faithfully accept and uphold it and practice according to its teaching. Monastics and laity who followed his teaching were very numerous; some recited the Amitabha Sutra ten thousand to five hundred thousand times, some daily recited the Buddha’s name from ten thousand to a hundred thousand times; among them, those who attained samādhi and were reborn in the Pure Land were so many that they could not be recorded or described. If Master Shandao had held that recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth, he need only have written the four words “recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth” and distributed them; why copy more than a hundred thousand fascicles of the Amitabha Sutra to distribute to his disciples and the faithful? Honen and his followers, Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others, recklessly preach “recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth”; this is a denial that single-mindedness undefiled invariably brings rebirth, and a denial of the Dharma gate praised and embraced by the buddhas of the ten directions (which of course includes Amitābha Buddha of the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss). (For details see the article
“Master Honen Distorts the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception”
These people
slander the Buddha and destroy the Dharma; their karmic offenses reach the heavens! You must never
be taken in and deceived.
Question: In Master Honen’s

Dharma Sayings, Master Honen says: “The karma of settled certainty is precisely reciting the Buddha’s name; recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth, because it depends on the Buddha’s original vow.” Is that so?
Answer: In the Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra in Four Fascicles, Master Shandao teaches:
Single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting
the name of Amitābha, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, regardless of whether the time be long or short,
never forsaking it
thought after thought—this is called the karma of settled certainty, because it accords with that Buddha’s vow.”

“Single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting” means: reciting the Buddha’s name with single-minded focus. “Never forsaking it thought after thought” means: every single thought is a thought of Buddha-recitation; if one gives rise to idle thoughts, then one has forsaken the thought of Buddha-recitation. Therefore Master Shandao says: reciting the Buddha’s name with single-minded focus, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, regardless of whether the time be long or short, never forsaking the thought of Buddha-recitation thought after thought—this is called the karma of settled certainty, and it accords with Amitābha Buddha’s original vow. Thus in this teaching Master Shandao particularly emphasizes “single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting, never forsaking it thought after thought”; only this is the karma of settled certainty, only this accords with the Buddha’s original vow. Yet Master Honen actually chopped off “
single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting
” and “
never forsaking it thought after thought
,” and altered it into: “The karma of settled certainty is precisely reciting the Buddha’s name; recitation of the name invariably brings rebirth, because it depends on the Buddha’s original vow.”
Is this how one inherits Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought?!
Question: In Master Honen’s
Dharma Sayings, Master Honen says: “Amitābha urges Buddha-recitation and the Buddha will surely come to welcome one; Śākyamuni urges Buddha-recitation and one will surely be reborn.” Is that so?
Answer: In the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception, Śākyamuni Buddha teaches:

“If there are good men or good women of pure faith who hear the name of the Buddha Immeasurable Life—immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable in merit—and the adornments of the merit of the Land of Ultimate Bliss; having heard it, they reflect on it for one day and night, or two or three, or four or five, or six or seven,
with uninterrupted mindfulness
. This
(these)
good men or good women, at the time of death, will be surrounded before and behind by the Buddha Immeasurable Life together with his immeasurable śrāvaka disciples and the assembly of bodhisattvas
coming to stand before them

, with compassion adding aid, so that their minds are not confused. Once they have abandoned life, they will follow the assembly of that Buddha and be born in the pure buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha Immeasurable Life.”

Here the World-Honored One clearly teaches: for good men or good women of uninterrupted mindfulness (single-mindedness undefiled), “at the time of death, the Buddha Immeasurable Life together with his immeasurable śrāvaka disciples and the assembly of bodhisattvas will surround them before and behind and come to stand before them.”
This passage of sutra means: because of uninterrupted mindfulness, Amitābha Buddha comes to stand before them. Therefore Śākyamuni Buddha teaches in this sutra:
with uninterrupted mindfulness, the Buddha will surely come to welcome one

. Yet Master Honen distorted the meaning of the sutra, saying: Śākyamuni Buddha urges and teaches that Buddha-recitation invariably brings rebirth (so long as one recites the Buddha’s name, one will surely be reborn). The Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception is praised and embraced by the buddhas of the ten directions, and of course also praised and embraced by Amitābha Buddha; therefore Amitābha Buddha also teaches:
with uninterrupted mindfulness, the Buddha will surely come to welcome one

. Yet Master Honen distorted it into: Amitābha urges and teaches that if one recites the Buddha’s name the Buddha will surely come to welcome one (so long as one recites the Buddha’s name, the Buddha will come to welcome one). Master Honen’s fallacy

denies that “uninterrupted mindfulness invariably brings rebirth,” and denies the Dharma gate praised and embraced by the buddhas of the ten directions (which of course includes Amitābha Buddha of the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss)
(for details see the article
“Master Honen Distorts the Sutra of Praising the Pure Land and the Buddha’s Reception”
! It slanders Śākyamuni Buddha and Amitābha Buddha!
Question: Master Honen says: “The rebirth of scattered-mind Buddha-recitation is precisely the supreme primal vow.” Is this so?
Answer: Let us look at how the Great Master Shandao taught. The Great Master Shandao said:
“Precisely because calling upon the Name is easy, continuous [recitation] brings rebirth. If one can
practice thought after thought continuing without break, taking the end of life as the limit
, then of ten, ten are reborn; of a hundred, a hundred are reborn. Why is this? Because free of external, scattered conditions, one gains right mindfulness
and thereby accords with the Buddha's primal vow
and because it does not violate the teaching and follows the Buddha's words.”
(See
“Continuous Recitation Brings Rebirth”

) Please note: the Great Master Shandao here instructed: “thought after thought continuing without break, taking the end of life as the limit” — this is what accords with the Buddha's primal vow, and therefore of ten, ten are reborn, of a hundred, a hundred are reborn. Yet Master Honen actually says “the rebirth of scattered-mind Buddha-recitation is precisely the supreme primal vow”!
Is this the way to inherit the Pure Land thought of the Great Master Shandao?!
The Great Master Shandao continued:
“If one abandons single-minded recitation and practices miscellaneous karma, then of a hundred, one or two may rarely be attained; of a thousand, three or four may rarely be attained. Why is this?
Because
scattered conditions stir and move [the mind]
(because the mind turns outward, grasping at all kinds of miscellaneous conditions)
, one loses right mindfulness
and does not accord with the Buddha's primal vow
because
, and because it violates the teaching and does not follow the Buddha's words
because the fixed thought does not continue
, because the mind does not continue in mindfulness to repay the Buddha's grace.”

This is to say: if the mind turns outward, grasping at all kinds of miscellaneous conditions, then it does not accord with the Buddha's primal vow. Is not scattered-mind Buddha-recitation precisely the case of not single-mindedly reciting, but of grasping after miscellaneous scattered conditions? Therefore, scattered-mind Buddha-recitation does not accord with the Buddha's primal vow.
Yet Master Honen actually says “the rebirth of scattered-mind Buddha-recitation is precisely the supreme primal vow”!
Is this the way to inherit the Pure Land thought of the Great Master Shandao?!
Question: It is said: rebirth depends entirely on the Buddha's power. Is this correct?
Answer: In the Four-Fascicle Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra, the Great Master Shandao said:
All good and evil ordinary beings who gain rebirth all do so by relying on the strength of the great vow and karma of Amitabha Buddha as the
strengthening condition

[Strengthening condition]All conditioned dharmas, in their arising, accomplishment, or result, have indirect causes; whatever possesses a dominant, powerful function and can serve as an aid for other dharmas to arise, be accomplished, or result is called a strengthening condition. For example, sunlight, rain, and dew are the strengthening condition for the growth of crops. The Great Vehicle Compendium of Meanings says: “As for the strengthening condition, because it functions powerfully in producing dharmas, it is called strengthening.” [Conditioned dharmas]All things that arise through the union of causes and conditions.

[Cause and conditions]For a thing's arising, the directly effective and strong one is the cause, and the indirect, weakly aiding one is the condition. For example, the seed is the cause, and rain, dew, and the farmer are the conditions; through the union of this cause and conditions, rice is produced.
Therefore
, the vast vow of Amitabha Buddha is the
strengthening condition
for all good and evil ordinary beings to gain rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. Then what is the cause? The
cause

for all good and evil ordinary beings to gain rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss is what our original teacher Sakyamuni Buddha proclaimed with his golden mouth, and what Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss praised and received, in the
Sutra of Praise on the Pure Land Buddha's Reception
as spoken:
“Faithfully receive and rouse the vow; cultivate as taught.”
When cause and conditions unite and the response and the way intersect, then one accomplishes rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
[Faithfully receive and rouse the vow; cultivate as taught]In the Sutra of Praise on the Pure Land Buddha's Reception, the Buddha said:

“If there are good men or good women of pure faith who, having heard of such inconceivable virtues and the name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life and the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss,
all should faithfully receive and rouse the vow, cultivate as taught, and be born in that Buddha-land
Please note: “
faithfully receive and rouse the vow, cultivate as taught, and be born in that Buddha-land
[Response and way intersect]The response of sentient beings and the power to respond of the Buddha intermingle with each other.

Yet Master Honen and his followers Master Huijing and Master Jingzong and others say: “Rebirth depends entirely on the Buddha's power.” They explain: “Rebirth depends entirely on the Buddha's power” means “Amitabha Buddha practices for us and bears our karmic offenses.”
Is this really so? Then why did Sakyamuni Buddha also say in the
Sutra of Praise on the Pure Land Buddha's Reception:
All should faithfully receive and rouse the vow,
cultivate as taught
, and be born in that Buddha-land
And why did he urge over and over again to
cultivate as taught
In the Sutra of Praise on the Pure Land Buddha's Reception, the World-Honored One instructed:

“If there are good men or good women of pure faith who, having heard of such inconceivable virtues and the name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life and the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, all should faithfully receive and rouse the vow,
cultivate as taught
, and be born in that Buddha-land.”
Those who cultivate as taught

will all surely attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and all will surely be born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life. Therefore, Sariputra. All you sentient beings should all
faithfully receive and understand the words of me and the World-Honored Buddhas of the ten directions
, and be diligent and vigorous,
cultivating as taught
, without giving rise to doubt.”
Those who cultivate as taught

will all surely attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and all will surely be born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life. Therefore, Sariputra. If there are good men or good women of pure faith, all should, with regard to the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, with deep mind have faith and understanding and rouse the vow to be reborn there,
and not act with laxity

“In this defiled, patient-enduring world, in the evil time of the five turbidities, if there are good men or good women of pure faith who, having heard of such Dharma extremely difficult to believe in all the world, are able to give rise to faith and understanding, receive, uphold, and proclaim it,
cultivating as taught

, you should know that this person is extremely rare, having planted wholesome roots before countless Buddhas. At the end of life, this person will surely be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, enjoying various meritorious, adorned, pure Buddha-land Mahayana Dharma-joys.”
Moreover, the Great Master Shandao, in the
The Great Master Shandao's Text on Right Mindfulness at the Moment of Death
, earnestly admonished:
The matter of life and death is great; one must put forth one's own effort to accomplish it.
A single mistaken thought brings suffering through kalpas — who can take your place?
Think on it! Think on it
In
“Where Master Honen Stumbled”
, we said:
Master Honen's stumbling point is that he
abandoned the Dharma-gate that Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss praised and received —
the Sutra of Praise on the Pure Land Buddha's Reception
Because Honen both feared arduous practice and coveted fame and profit
therefore not only did he not cultivate as taught in the Sutra of Praise on the Pure Land Buddha's Reception,
but on the contrary, by twisting the Sutra of Praise on the Pure Land Buddha's Reception (see the essay
“Master Honen Misinterpreted the Sutra of Praise on the Pure Land Buddha's Reception”
) and by fabricating the great-vow gate (see the essay
“Master Honen Fabricated the Great-Vow Gate”
), he built up for himself a teaching system that is both lazy and greedy.

[Both lazy and greedy]The lazy one is unwilling to cultivate arduously, even fearing arduous practice, vainly hoping for gain without labor; the greedy one covets fame, covets profit, covets the pleasures of desire, and covets the fruit-position.
How could one
call this lazy, greedy, and fabricated teaching system the Pure Land thought of the Great Master Shandao? This is simply a blasphemy against the Great Master Shandao!
